description: Candidate-level audit of the three canonical runs. One record per unique post-deduplication substantive candidate, with the complete claim text, its cited evidence, every pairwise NLI score, every guard result, and whether it reached the published report. Immutable: regenerate only by re-recording.
publication_rule: A claim publishes when at least one cited, citable quote passes every deterministic guard and entails the claim at or above the support threshold. Quotes are scored individually and never concatenated.

nist-ai-risk-framework.question: Using the official NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 publication as the primary source, explain how the framework structures AI risk management, including its core functions, governance role, and practical use. Support claims with page-level evidence from the NIST publication where available.

candidates.claim: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 defines four core functions: Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage.

evidence.quote: The framework is organized around four interconnected functions: Govern — establish policies, roles, and oversight for AI risk management; Map — understand AI systems in context, including intended use and impacts; Measure — assess and monitor AI system performance and trustworthiness over time; Manage — prioritize risks, implement mitigation strategies, and respond to incidents or changes.

A practical rollout typically looks like:
1. Adopt the Govern function at the organization layer — roles, policies, oversight, and approval gates.

3. Define Measure signals — evaluations, red-teaming, and monitoring with thresholds and owners.
4. Run Manage as a continuous loop — prioritize, treat, accept residual risk, respond to incidents.

candidates.claim: Pinecone uses serverless object storage with $0.33/GB/month storage pricing.

evidence.quote:
Pinecone: Serverless + Dedicated Read Nodes
Pinecone eliminated pod-based pricing in 2024 and migrated all workloads to serverless object storage architecture. The pricing structure has three levers verified from pinecone.io/pricing (March 2026):
- Storage: $0.33/GB/month. At 10M 1,536-dim vectors (float32): ~58GB raw → with 1.5x HNSW overhead = ~87GB → $28.71/month storage.
- Read Units (RUs): $16/million on Standard, $24/million on Enterprise. A query consumes 1 RU per 1GB of namespace. Minimum 0.25 RU per query regardless of namespace size.
- Write Units (WUs): Billed for upsert, update, delete operations. Exact per-unit rate varies by region and provider. Plan minimums: Standard $50/month, Enterprise $500/month.
- Dedicated Read Nodes (DRN): Per-node hourly billing. Verified production benchmark: 135M vectors at 600 QPS, P50 45ms, P99 96ms (December 2025 release notes). 1.4B vectors at 5,700 QPS, P99 60ms (official customer benchmark).

candidates.withhold_reason: entailed by S2-e2 at 1.000 >= 0.98
